mechanism.name: Wang and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2018) binary odds-product algebraic causal completion

generation_equations.label: Baseline and latent distribution
generation_equations.expression: X=(1,X2); X2 uniform on (-1,-0.5) union (0.5,1), density 1; U~Bernoulli(0.5), independent of X2 (explicit adaptation). Individuals iid.

generation_equations.label: Eq6 and Eq7 mapping
generation_equations.expression: Let B=q(2-d)+d. F(d,q)=[B-sqrt(B^2+4q(1-d)(1-q))]/[2(q-1)]=2q(1-d)/[B+sqrt(B^2+4q(1-d)(1-q))]. For q=1, F(d,1)=(1-d)/2. p0D=F(deltaD,OPD), p0Y=F(deltaD*delta,OPY).

generation_equations.label: Source outcome marginal
generation_equations.expression: Y|Z,X,U ~ Bernoulli(p0Y(X)+Z deltaD(X)delta(X)+0.1(2U-1)), recovered by the explicit causal completion below. No probability clipping.

generation_equations.label: Algebraic causal completion adaptation
generation_equations.expression: rD=p0D+0.1(2U-1), rY=p0Y+0.1(2U-1), t=delta(X); independent V_Z,V_D,V_Y~Uniform(0,1), independent of X,U. Z=1{V_Z<expit(gamma^T X)}, D(z)=1{V_D<rD+z deltaD}, g_a=rY-t*rD+a*t, Y(a)=1{V_Y<g_a}. Observe D=D(Z), Y=Y(D). Then E[Y|Z,X,U]=g0+P(D=1|Z,X,U)*(g1-g0)=rY+Z deltaD*t. E[Y(1)-Y(0)|X,U]=t.

generation_equations.label: Population target
generation_equations.expression: Delta_W=integral_{-1}^{-0.5} tanh(0.1+0.5x) dx + integral_{0.5}^{1} tanh(0.1+0.5x) dx; antiderivative 2 log cosh(0.1+0.5x).

evidence.expression: independent V_Z,V_D,V_Y~Uniform(0,1), independent of X,U. Z=1{V_Z<expit(gamma^T X)}, D(z)=1{V_D<rD+z deltaD}, g_a=rY-t*rD+a*t, Y(a)=1{V_Y<g_a}. Observe D=D(Z), Y=Y(D). Then E[Y|Z,X,U]=g0+P(D=1|Z,X,U)*(g1-g0)=rY+Z deltaD*t. E[Y(1)-Y(0)|X,U]=t.

independent V_Z,V_D,V_Y~Uniform(0,1), independent of X,U. Z=1{V_Z<expit(gamma^T X)}, D(z)=1{V_D<rD+z deltaD}, g_a=rY-t*rD+a*t, Y(a)=1{V_Y<g_a}. Observe D=D(Z), Y=Y(D). Then E[Y|Z,X,U]=g0+P(D=1|Z,X,U)*(g1-g0)=rY+Z deltaD*t. E[Y(1)-Y(0)|X,U]=t.

sampling.dependence: iid units. X2,U,V_Z,V_D,V_Y independent; U binary, V_Z,V_D,V_Y independent Uniform(0,1). Z depends on X2; D on X2,Z,U,V_D; potential Y(a) on X2,U,V_Y. Shared V_Y couples Y(0),Y(1). Only Y=Y(D) is observed; U and uniforms hidden.

assumptions: iid individuals, X2 uniform on (-1,-0.5) union (0.5,1), U independent Bernoulli(0.5), conditional instrument overlap and nonzero deltaD on both intervals
Independent potential-response uniform V_Y and treatment uniform V_D, both independent of X,U and instrument innovation; consistency Y=Y(D), iid units and no interference
The adapted Y(a) depends on a,X,U,V_Y only, establishing exclusion; Z independent of U given X; Y(a) independent of D,Z given X,U by independent innovations

Conditional mean treatment effect g1-g0=delta(X) does not depend on U (A5.b); treatment mean difference deltaD(X) does not depend on U (A5.a). These are derived for our explicit completion, not asserted source structural equations
No monotonicity or causal LATE claim; deltaD changes sign between intervals

properties.notes: One active continuous baseline X2; intercept is implicit. tanh mean contrasts, exp odds products, logistic instrument propensity, and Z*deltaD(X)*delta(X) outcome interaction. U enters both conditional probabilities additively.

estimand.name: ATE
estimand.definition: Population causal ATE E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the explicitly adapted algebraic causal completion = E[tanh(0.1+0.5 X2)] = average conditional Wald ratio. Binary intervention a=1 versus a=0, full iid superpopulation; not a LATE.

truth.expression: Population causal ATE E[Y(1)-Y(0)] in the explicitly adapted algebraic causal completion = E[tanh(0.1+0.5 X2)] = average conditional Wald ratio. Binary intervention a=1 versus a=0, full iid superpopulation; not a LATE.
truth.derivation: Analytic log-cosh integral over two intervals with total length one; independent root-inversion and adaptive quadrature in verify.py

adaptations: Algebraic causal completion adaptation: rD=p0D+kappa(2U-1), rY=p0Y+kappa(2U-1), t=delta(X); D(z)=1{V_D<rD+z*deltaD}, Y(a)=1{V_Y<rY-t*rD+a*t}, using independent Uniform(0,1) V_D,V_Y. This constructed coupling recovers source conditional Bernoulli marginals, is not an author-specified coupling, and adds no numeric coefficients.
Set U independent of X; use independent random innovations across individuals and generation stages. The source gives U marginal Bernoulli(0.5) without an explicit X-U coupling.

Target the causal ATE of our explicitly constructed completion, which algebraically equals the source average Wald functional. Causal interpretation is for this adaptation, not a claim that the paper specified this potential-outcome construction.
Rationalize Eqs.(6),(7) for numerical stability, including the continuous q=1 limit; coefficients unchanged.

Return X2,Z,D,Y only; implicit intercept omitted. Accept arbitrary n and seed instead of the source n=500 and 1000 estimator repetitions. Omit analyst misspecification covariates and estimator comparisons because they do not alter this DGP.
